statement: Let rho be any positive 4x4 phase-covariant state with correlated block A>=0 and offdiagonal-basis diagonal entries p_ij>=0. Choose any finite rank-one decomposition A=sum_l z_l z_l^*, and for each unordered pair e={i,j} put s_e=sum_l |(z_l)_i (z_l)_j| and q_e=sqrt(p_ij*p_ji). For each of the three perfect matchings M set m_M=min(1, min_(e in M,s_e>0) q_e/s_e), with an empty inner minimum interpreted as infinity. If sum_M m_M>=1, then rho has an explicit Schmidt-rank<=2 decomposition. No PPT or phase-balance hypothesis is required. A decomposition-independent sufficient condition replaces s_e by sqrt(A_ii*A_jj).
construction: Let S=sum_M m_M>=1 and alpha_M=m_M/S, so sum_M alpha_M=1 and alpha_M*s_e<=q_e for every edge e in M. For each matching M and each vector z_l, define a 4x4 coefficient matrix X_lM as two disjoint 2x2 rank-one blocks. Its diagonal entries are sqrt(alpha_M)*(z_l)_i. On each matched pair e={i,j} with nonzero |z_i*z_j| choose t_e>0 with t_e^2=sqrt(p_ij/p_ji), and set X_ij=sqrt(alpha_M)*t_e*sqrt(|z_i*z_j|), X_ji=sqrt(alpha_M)*z_i*z_j/(t_e*sqrt(|z_i*z_j|)). Each block determinant is zero. If alpha_M=0 omit this atom; if a directed p vanishes, the inequality alpha_M*s_e<=q_e=0 ensures every relevant product z_i*z_j vanishes, so set both offdiagonals to zero. Thus rank(X_lM)<=2 in all cases.
coefficient_check: Twirling [X_lM] under diagonal U tensor conjugate(U) keeps the correlated block alpha_M*z_l*z_l^* and makes each offdiagonal basis population its squared coefficient. For e={i,j} in M, summing l gives alpha_M*t_e^2*s_e<=p_ij and alpha_M*t_e^(-2)*s_e<=p_ji by alpha_M*s_e<=sqrt(p_ij*p_ji). Each unordered edge lies in exactly one perfect matching, so there is no double allocation. Summing M,l recovers A and produces no offdiagonal population exceeding p; add the remaining nonnegative (p_ij-p'_ij)[|ij>] product projectors. A discrete U=diag(1,i^a,i^b,i^c) twirl with 4^3 choices is exact, since all nontrivial phase-character exponents have magnitude <=2. Taking the spectral decomposition of A uses at most four z_l, so at most 3*4*64 rank-two orbit terms plus 12 product-diagonal terms suffice.
simple_all_variable_corollary: Cauchy-Schwarz gives s_ij<=sqrt(A_ii*A_jj). Hence one may use the decomposition-independent caps m_M^diag=min(1, min_(ij in M,A_ii*A_jj>0) sqrt(p_ij*p_ji/(A_ii*A_jj))); if their sum is at least one, rho has Schmidt number at most 2. In particular, when A_ii=a for all i and sqrt(p_ij*p_ji)>=a/3 for every pair, the conclusion holds, regardless of the phases of A or whether rho is PPT.
application: The intrinsically frustrated PPT-entangled rho(1,1/2,1/2)/10 from frontier-20261028-conference-ppt-sn2-family-v1.json SHA256 0812417dae661522d94c948d210699e9aadc116578d41b54fcd020e1c3a92340 satisfies the diagonal cap with all m_M=1/2, so this different construction also proves its SN<=2; that source separately proves entanglement. This certificate applies far beyond that symmetric family.
limits: The cap is sufficient, not necessary, and failure does not imply Schmidt number>=3. The state must have exactly the phase-covariant block structure, and the rank-two matching construction is specific to four diagonal indices. The proof is all-variable WRITTEN reasoning with an explicit finite decomposition; no independent/formal review or novelty claim.
